roles.title: Speech recognition
roles.description: Listens to the video and writes down what is said, with the time of every word. Used in every dub. The choice is remembered per dub, so changing the default never touches finished work.

roles.title: Translation
roles.description: Translates the English text into Slovak line by line and keeps each line short enough for its time slot. Runs inside Ollama, which stores its models for all programs on this PC.

roles.title: Slovak voice
roles.description: Speaks the Slovak text. There is one model with ten voices (F1 to M5); you pick the voice for each dub.

roles.title: Speaker detection
roles.description: Optional. Tells speakers apart so each can get a voice of their own.

roles.title: Speech removal
roles.description: Optional. Separates speech from music and effects, so the music can stay under the dub.

roles.title: Voice cloning
roles.description: Optional. Shifts the Slovak voice towards the timbre of the original speaker. Only for voices you may imitate.

roles.title: Tools and packages
roles.description: Programs and libraries (not AI models) that optional features need.

entries.title: Whisper large-v3
entries.summary: The most accurate speech recognition we tested, and the default.
choose_if: You have an NVIDIA graphics card with 6 GB or more.
You want the best result on accents, background noise and fast speech.
avoid_if: You have no NVIDIA card: it still works on the processor, but much more slowly.

requirements.note: About 3.9 GB of GPU memory while it works; released again afterwards.

entries.measured: Word-perfect on our test clips; about 0.06 to 0.09 times real time on an RTX 5060 laptop (a 5-minute video in 31 s).

entries.title: Whisper large-v3 turbo
entries.summary: About half the size and faster than large-v3; slightly less accurate on difficult audio.
choose_if: You want faster recognition or have only 4 to 6 GB of GPU memory.
Your videos have clear speech.
avoid_if: Your videos are noisy, have heavy accents or music under the speech: use large-v3.

entries.title: Whisper small (English only)
entries.summary: A small model for weak computers. English only, noticeably less accurate.
choose_if: Your computer has no NVIDIA card or little memory.
You only dub English and want the smallest download.
avoid_if: You want the best result: the large models are much more accurate.

entries.title: NVIDIA Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3
entries.summary: A fast alternative from NVIDIA. Runs on the processor, so the graphics card stays free. Understands 25 European languages.
choose_if: You want fast recognition without using the GPU.
You plan to dub from a language other than English (it lists Slovak and Czech among its languages).
avoid_if: You want the most proven option: Whisper large-v3 is what LocalDub was tested with.

requirements.note: Uses the processor through ONNX (sherpa-onnx); no PyTorch needed.

entries.measured: On 4 English clips (44 s to 5.7 min) its text differs from Whisper large-v3 in 0 to 6% of words, mostly punctuation and where sentences end. It misheard rare names ("Palak Paneer" became "Palek Paner"). On this laptop it was not faster than Whisper (both about 0.4 times real time on balanced power). Other languages were not tested.

entries.title: TranslateGemma 4B
entries.summary: Google's translation model, small and quick. The default and what every test video was dubbed with.
choose_if: You have 6 GB or more of GPU memory, or just want it to be quick.
You are not sure: start here.
avoid_if: You have a 12 GB or larger card and want to try a more accurate (slower) translation.
entries.measured: About 0.3 s per line once loaded; plain, usually correct Slovak. Idioms are translated literally and long lines have to be shortened.

entries.title: TranslateGemma 12B
entries.summary: The larger sibling of the default. Normally better with idioms and long sentences, but slower and needs a bigger graphics card.
choose_if: You have an NVIDIA card with 12 GB or more (for example an RTX 5070 Ti with 16 GB).
Translation quality matters more to you than speed.
avoid_if: Your card has 8 GB or less: only part of the model fits and it becomes slow.

entries.title: TranslateGemma 27B
entries.summary: The largest TranslateGemma. For workstation graphics cards.
choose_if: You have an NVIDIA card with 24 GB or more.

entries.title: Qwen3 8B
entries.summary: A general-purpose model from Alibaba. Kept for comparison; not recommended for Slovak.
choose_if: You want to compare it yourself.
avoid_if: You want reliable Slovak: in our benchmark it mistranslated idioms and produced several nonsensical lines.
entries.measured: 12-line benchmark (docs/translation_benchmark.md): several wrong or nonsensical lines, 2.7 times slower to load than TranslateGemma 4B.

entries.title: Supertonic 3
entries.summary: The Slovak voice: ten voices (five female, five male), fast on the processor.
choose_if: It is required: there is no other Slovak voice in LocalDub.

requirements.note: Runs on the processor (about 6x faster than real time with 4 threads).

entries.measured: All Slovak letters are supported. Speech made with it is marked as AI-generated in the exported file, as the licence requires.
entries.pinned: Pinned to one revision because the upstream project has been archived.

entries.title: Speaker detection (pyannote + 3D-Speaker)
entries.summary: Splits the dialogue by speaker and guesses male or female from the pitch. Runs on the processor.
choose_if: Your video has two or more people talking.
You know how many speakers there are (give the number, it is much more reliable).
avoid_if: There is a single speaker: it adds nothing.

license.name: MIT (pyannote) / Apache-2.0 toolkit (3D-Speaker weights: not stated)

entries.measured: 10 of 10 lines right on a synthetic three-voice dialogue; not verified on real recordings.
entries.pinned: Two files, each pinned to a SHA-256.

entries.title: Demucs htdemucs
entries.summary: Removes the original speech but keeps the music and effects.
choose_if: The video has music or effects you want to keep under the Slovak dub.
avoid_if: The video is just talking: the plain 'quiet' or 'mute' options are enough.

license.name: MIT (code); the weights' licence was not checked

entries.measured: Removed all original speech from a clip with background music (no words recognised in the music stem).

entries.title: OpenVoice V2 converter
entries.summary: Makes the Slovak voice sound more like the original speaker.
choose_if: You dub your own videos, or voices you have permission to imitate.
avoid_if: You do not have the speaker's permission.
entries.measured: Voice similarity to the original speaker rose from 0.05 to 0.51 and from 0.30 to 0.44 (speaker-embedding cosine); whether it sounds natural has not been judged.

entries.title: YouTube import tools (yt-dlp and Deno)
entries.summary: Lets you paste a YouTube link instead of choosing a file.
choose_if: You dub videos from YouTube that you have the right to download.
entries.pinned: Not pinned on purpose: yt-dlp must follow YouTube's changes. Update it from the YouTube form.

entries.title: Optional packages (PyTorch and Demucs)
entries.summary: The libraries that speech removal and voice cloning need.
choose_if: You want speech removal or voice cloning.
avoid_if: You do not: they are large and nothing else needs them.

requirements.note: About 2.9 GB to download, 4.5 GB on disk.

license.name: BSD-style (PyTorch); NVIDIA CUDA parts under NVIDIA's licence

entries.pinned: Versions come from the program's lock file.
